title: Why every list item needs a key

slides.say: Rendering a list without keys gives a warning: each child in a list should have a unique key prop. Here is why.

slides.text: Imagine files with no names, only "first", "second". Delete one and everything shifts.
slides.say: Imagine your desktop files had no names. Only first file, second file. Delete one, and every position shifts. Confusing.
A key is like a file name. A string or number that identifies the item among its siblings, even when the list is reordered.

slides.text: JSX directly inside map() always needs a key, unique among siblings.
slides.say: Rule: JSX elements directly inside a map call always need keys. They must be unique among siblings, but can repeat in a different array.
